findings.text: follow-on: the module docstring attributes the observed defect to a role ("the noise a lead read on 2026-10-14"), provenance the repository bans from source comments and docstrings; state the mechanism instead.

follow-on: take_lift_claim creates the claim before the row reaches the pane, so a follower that dies or whose delivery fails in that window leaves a standing claim that blocks every other follower of the session from drawing that transition for up to LIFT_CLAIM_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (24h); a shorter bound or a delivery-checked claim would bound the loss.

follow-on: take_lift_claim re-implements the exclusive-create claim pattern the repository already owns at reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:526 (O_EXCL with staleness reclaim) without extending or wrapping it, so the two can drift.

follow-on: the base arm's own `module.__file__` line names the head worktree's reckon/crew/ticker.py, not the base tree its header and the manifest's measurement_module name, so the record does not show which revision the base arm imported.

item_verdicts.diff: read the two commits against base 931406cc1dce0caa4108514f048c108422cf0dd2; five files changed inside the declared scope, adding the lift_id field, the lift_claim seam, the claim helpers and their tests.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for a temp-crew-home test running three followers of one session over three streams carrying the same lift-granted and lift-ended row, exactly one grant and one end across their output, a second lift id drawing its own row, another session drawing on its own claim, the claim's shape and pruning, and the negative control; tests/test_a_lift_is_drawn_once_per_pane.py:1 implements each of those cases.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to draw each lift row once per session pane by sharing one exclusive-create claim across the session's project followers, and reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:930 take_lift_claim with the RowPolicy._feed_lift seam at reckon/crew/ticker.py:1705 delivers exactly that, matching plan §23's deliverable.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records tests/test_a_lift_is_drawn_once_per_pane.py 10/10, head 725 passed 0 failed, base 713 passed 2 failed, and names head-gate.log, base-gate.log and negative-control.log.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the source node was fenced to reckon/crew/lift_watch.py, reckon/crew/ticker.py, reckon/crew_follow_commands.py, tests/test_a_lift_is_drawn_once_per_pane.py, the evidence fragment and the figure directory, and every path in the diff is inside them.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_lift_is_drawn_once_per_pane.py:109 asserts exactly one grant across three followers, an independent count over their printed output, and negative-control.log records it reddening when the claim is dropped in RowPolicy._feed_lift.
justifications.evidence: the two arm logs and the named test are recorded in the manifest, but base-gate.log's own `module.__file__` line names the head worktree's reckon/crew/ticker.py rather than the base tree its own header and the manifest's measurement_module name, so the base arm's recorded instrument does not reconcile.
justifications.fit: the seam, helpers and comments state the mechanism in the surrounding idiom, but tests/test_a_lift_is_drawn_once_per_pane.py:8 names "a lead" as the observer, a role attribution the source rules forbid in comments and docstrings.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1017 binds the claim to the follower's own session and reckon/crew/ticker.py:1705 takes it at the print point, so a session's followers draw one row per (session, lift id, transition).
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:947 opens its own O_CREAT|O_EXCL claim beside the existing claim owner reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:526 and the atomic-create helper reckon/_store.py:449, extending neither.
justifications.scope_discipline: all five changed paths sit inside the six declared write paths, the figure directory left unused, and no path outside them is touched.
